stories.title: OpenAI Urges California to Strengthen Its AI Safety Bill
stories.summary: OpenAI has publicly asked California lawmakers to make the state's pending AI safety bill stronger, not weaker. Engadget and TechCrunch both reported the call. OpenAI did not previously push this hard for tougher rules on its own industry.
stories.whyItMatters: State AI rules could set a template for the rest of the US. OpenAI's stance shows how AI labs are trying to shape regulation instead of just reacting to it.
whatToWatch: Whether California lawmakers amend the bill before a vote
Whether other states follow California's approach
questions: Which specific provisions does OpenAI want strengthened?
Does this signal a broader shift in OpenAI's regulatory strategy?

stories.title: US Battery Startups Find a Lifeline in Defense Contracts
stories.summary: TechCrunch reports that US battery startups are turning to defense-sector funding and contracts to stay afloat. This suggests commercial battery demand alone has not been enough to sustain some companies. The defense sector is stepping in as an alternative source of capital.
stories.whyItMatters: Battery technology underpins EVs, grid storage, and consumer electronics. Defense money reshapes who survives in that supply chain and on whose terms.
whatToWatch: New defense contracts or funding rounds for battery startups
Whether commercial demand for these batteries recovers
questions: How dependent are these startups becoming on government money?

stories.title: What Would It Take for Waymo to Reach Level 5 Automation?
stories.summary: Engadget examines the gap between Waymo's current Level 4 self-driving cars and full Level 5 automation. Level 4 vehicles operate autonomously only within set conditions or areas. Level 5 would mean no limits and no human backup at all.
stories.whyItMatters: The distance between Level 4 and Level 5 defines how far robotaxi companies still have to go, and shapes expectations for when driverless cars can operate anywhere.
whatToWatch: Whether Waymo or a competitor announces progress toward Level 5
Any regulatory changes tied to automation levels
questions: Is Level 5 technically achievable soon, or mostly a theoretical benchmark?
